newsitem.title: CONGO: Confusion over Kabila location delays Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: Confusion over Kabila location delays Zaire talks.

text.p: Zairean peace talks aboard a South African ship in Congo were delayed on Wednesday by confusion over where to pick up rebel leader Laurent Kabila, United Nations envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said.
Sahnoun told reporters aboard the navy icebreaker Outeniqua he expected the talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko and South African President Nelson Mandela to begin "within a few hours".

South African Defence Minister Joe Modise told reporters he had flown south in the ship's helicopter to Soyo in Zaire, but heard later that Kabila was waiting in the Angolan enclave of Cabinda, south of Pointe Noire where the ship was docked.
Mobutu arrived by air from Kinshasa slightly after the scheduled 11 a.m. (1000 gmt) start of the talks, in which Kabila is likely to demand his immediate resignation.
Mandela, who flew into Congo earlier to chair the second face-to-face meeting between the Zairean rivals, was waiting ashore with Congo President Pascal Lissouba.
Officials said on Tuesday South Africa had hammered out the "skeleton" of an agreement on a transition to democracy, which they hoped Mobutu and Kabila would ratify.
